install_opencode_runtime.py is invoked from the Railway [build] buildCommand (deploy build time), not from a preDeploy bootstrap, so it never mounts or accesses the /data volume; it writes only the pinned binary under /app/bin. The startup seam (railway_issuer_startup.py) now also exposes the runtime vendor dir on the import path before its lazy bootstrap import, then keeps the volume-aware check, signing-key scrub, and issuer exec sequencing unchanged.

findings.evidence: Runtime-integrity gate: the installer must refuse to install anything but the exact pinned archive. Verified: _download() verifies the SHA-256 after streaming and raises OpenCodeInstallError on mismatch; _verify_platform() and single-member extraction fail closed; main() returns 2 and installs nothing on any failure, so a tampered or unreachable release aborts the build rather than starting with an untrusted binary.

Atomic, standalone installation: the extracted binary must not be partially installed or left executable mid-write. Verified: extraction writes only the single `opencode` regular member to a .tmp sibling then os.replace(); chmod 0o755 is applied before replace, and no archive path is ever traversed, so no foreign artifact or partial binary survives.

Sandbox visibility of the pinned runtime (P1 #1): the adapter previously exec'd the host path inside the bwrap sandbox, which mounts /usr,/bin,/lib,/lib64,/etc but not /app, so a host-resolved /app/bin/opencode was invisible to dispatch. Verified resolved: _sandbox_executable_path remaps executables that live under the sandbox or credential home, reuses any executable already under a mounted system path, and otherwise ro-binds exactly the one resolved file read-only into the dedicated /opt/hunter/bin mount point; _sandbox_command execs the in-sandbox path. Five focused regression tests pin the mount construction, the reuse branches, and the final argv.

Host-side provisioning of the runtime (runbook): on the deployed image the pinned binary lives at /app/bin/opencode and the adapter resolves it via HUNTER_OPENCODE_EXECUTABLE (default 'opencode') through PATH lookup. If the operator does not set HUNTER_OPENCODE_EXECUTABLE=/app/bin/opencode or add /app/bin to PATH, the first dispatch fails closed with 'OpenCode executable is unavailable'. Safe because fail-closed, but the deployment runbook must record the provisioning step before first dispatch.

Railway vendor import path (P1 #2): railway.toml installs Hunter via `pip install . --target /app/vendor`, which is not on the interpreter's default import path. Verified resolved: _ensure_runtime_import_paths() inserts the configured vendor dir (default /app/vendor, override HUNTER_RUNTIME_VENDOR_DIR) at the front of sys.path before the lazy bootstrap import and exports the merged PYTHONPATH so the exec'd issuer child inherits it; absent dir is a no-op followed by fail-closed bootstrap. Three focused regression tests pin the prepend, the no-op, and a vendor module import.

The download in _download() streams the archive without a content-length cap before verifying SHA-256. Because the URL is a pinned immutable GitHub release and the digest is verified before any install, the worst case is bounded build-time disk usage; a size cap or redirect policy check is suggested hardening, not a current safety defect.

The in-sandbox dispatch requires the pinned binary to be self-contained or depend only on the sandbox-mounted prefixes (/usr,/bin,/lib,/lib64,/etc,/proc,/dev). The pinned asset is a compiled release and the mount coverage is in place, but this is provable only on the target image; the deploy smoke step should confirm the first sandboxed dispatch before production use. Fail-closed if the binary cannot exec.
